input.quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: The assignment clause in § (h) gives AP (and Kubient) the right to assign without consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, with all other assignments subject to consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. That is the mutual successor-assignment/reasonable-consent structure of our fallback position, and the M&A carve-out we require for AP is expressly present. There is no change-of-control provision anywhere in the document, so Kubient has no termination or re-pricing right on an AP change of control (searches for "change of control" and "merger" return nothing else). Short of the preferred position only in two minor respects — the consent restriction is symmetrical rather than one-way, and there is no express bar on assignment to an AP competitor — which we note but do not redline. The "non-transferable, non-assignable" language in the § 2 license grant is a scope-of-licence limitation, not an assignment restriction, and is governed by § (h).
